   "why_every_version_executes_it": "preview1 has no clone, splice or copy call, so all file data must enter linear memory via fd_read",

   "max_cores": 1},
  {"operator": "fd_write of all bytes from linear memory to DST",
   "component": "WASI fd_write",
   "frozen": true,
   "why_every_version_executes_it": "the only admissible way to put data into DST; a hard link is not a copy",
   "least_work": {"amount": 536870912, "unit": "bytes", "per_unit_cost_us": 0.000125, "total_ms": 67.1,
                  "calling_context": "1 MiB buffers at a measured 8 GB/s; not shown to be the minimum over all contexts"},
   "max_cores": 1}
 ],
 "floor_ms": 67.1,
 "L_delta": 2.635,
 "rationale": "C1 holds: every version must pass 512 MiB through frozen fd_read and fd_write, single-threaded. C2 is not established: 8 GB/s was measured only with 1 MiB buffers, and faster contexts were not tested. A floor of about 67 ms would give a log gap of 2.64, far above b=0.236. A bound on the minimum per-byte cost is still needed before claiming architectural."}
